d.d: To frighten or cause hesitation; to daunt, put off (usually used in the negative); to disconcert, to perturb.
d.x: Jumping out of an airplane does not faze him, yet he is afraid to ride a roller coaster.

d.d: Hesitant, frightened; daunted, disconcerted; perturbed, put off.
simple past and past participle of faze
